title: Common Post-Trip Regret Patterns
content: Traveler regret patterns from migration-focused trips: 1. We did not see a crossing (40% of crossing-focused travelers). Cause: Unrealistic expectations, insufficient time. Mitigation: Frame crossings as possible bonus, not goal. 2. Too many vehicles (30% of peak season travelers). Cause: August timing without concession budget. Mitigation: Discuss crowd tolerance before booking. 3. We should have stayed longer (25% of short trips). Cause: Transit consumes days, leaving insufficient migration time. Mitigation: Minimum 8 days for migration focus. 4. We missed calving for crossings (15% of return visitors). Cause: Marketing emphasis on crossings over calving. Mitigation: Present calving as equal option. 5. It was more expensive than we expected (20%). Cause: Peak season premium not clearly communicated. Mitigation: Transparent cost framing upfront.
